clue.text: Dr Johnson's "liquor for boys" suits a girl to a T!

parts.note: Clare is a girl's name
taken as written, the letter from 'to a T'

explanation.surface: A quotation from Samuel Johnson about a drink is said to suit some young woman perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson famously said claret is the liquor for boys, port for men and brandy for heroes; 'to a T' supplies the final letter after the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson's dictum ranked this red Bordeaux wine as the drink fit only for youths.

clue.text: Even serving men wear this

explanation.surface: Soldiers on duty all dress alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means consistent throughout, and the second part describes the regulation outfit worn by servicemen.

clue.text: Allowance to cut without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cut word wraps round the hesitation

parts.note: to lance is to cut open
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: An instruction to make an incision straight away, with no dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is a permitted margin of variation, a leeway or allowance in engineering terms.

clue.text: Take up residence and make payment

explanation.surface: Someone moves into a new home and pays the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to make one's home somewhere, and also to pay off a debt or account.

clue.text: Being angelic, keep quiet about cut-back

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hush sits round the turned cut

parts.note: sh is the call to keep quiet

indicators.note: back in cut-back tells us to read the word for cut backwards

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: Someone being saintly declines to mention a reduction in spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-back' reads as a noun for a reduction in spending, but splits into the word for cut and 'back', its reversal signal; 'about' puts it inside the call for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of heavenly beings in the angelic hierarchy.

clue.text: General cleaning

explanation.surface: A military officer is doing the housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping means wide-ranging or broad, and it is also brushing a floor clean with a broom.

clue.text: Managed the church stock-farm

parts.note: ran as in ran a business, managed it

explanation.surface: Someone was in charge of the parish's livestock holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm for raising cattle or other livestock, especially in North America.

clue.text: The mocker from Port Said

indicators.note: the answer is made out of these letters, rearranged from the place name

explanation.surface: A satirist hails from the Egyptian city at the mouth of the Suez Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parodist imitates others' work to ridicule it, so is a mocker.

clue.text: His very existence is dependent on British capital

definitions.text: His very existence is dependent on British capital

parts.words: His very existence is dependent on British capital
parts.note: reads like a man relying on money invested in Britain, but describes someone defined by living in the capital city

explanation.surface: A man whose livelihood relies entirely on British investment money.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of the UK's capital city is identified as such only by where he lives.

clue.text: Dicky, an older man

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, suggesting the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman with a weak heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name for the man, but is British slang for unreliable or weak ('a dicky heart') and works as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard is a man's first name.

clue.text: Sack for taking money in general

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the word for general takes in the money

parts.note: rife means widespread or general
L stands for pound, the British unit of money

explanation.surface: Dismissal awaits anyone pocketing cash in general circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from Latin libra, the pound sign, as in L.S.D.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle or sack a place is to ransack and plunder it.

clue.text: Hiding brilliance is a cover-up

parts.note: sounds like concealing talent, but literally describes a covering that screens a bright light

explanation.surface: Concealing one's genius amounts to a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: This fitting goes over a bulb to soften and conceal its glare.

clue.text: Put questions like keen beginner

parts.note: as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Quizzing someone in the manner of an eager novice.
explanation.definitionFit: To query someone is to pose inquiries to them.

clue.text: Steer car erratically and domestic rows result!

indicators.note: driving erratically suggests the letters swerve into a new order

explanation.surface: Bad driving causes household arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic rows' looks like family quarrels; it means lines of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Terraces are rows of joined houses, a common British form of housing.

clue.text: Fairly modern quarters to pine for

parts.note: north and east are two quarters of the compass
to wish for is to pine or long for

explanation.surface: Someone longs for up-to-date living accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish softens new, giving recent-ish or not old.

clue.text: Rose is exceptionally elegant in appearance

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A flower looks unusually refined.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweet briar, a wild species of the flower.

clue.text: Having sent up bouquet, go on about it. Sound off!

indicators.note: go on about it: the word for nagging surrounds the turned scent

parts.note: to rate someone is to scold or go on at them

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a wine's nose is its bouquet or aroma

explanation.surface: After smelling the flowers, someone is told to keep talking and then shout out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns the scent word upwards in this down clue, and 'about' places it within the scolding word; 'rate' meaning to scold is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To resonate is to ring out or reverberate loudly.

clue.text: Study is about over

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
on can mean over, as in a lid on (over) a jar

explanation.surface: A piece of research is nearly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To con is an old word meaning to learn or peruse carefully.

clue.text: Royal Navy canoed round the guns

indicators.note: turned round suggests the letters are mixed about

explanation.surface: Sailors paddled a small boat past the artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military artillery and munitions, the heavy weaponry collectively.

clue.text: Food eaten at breakfast say — good start, that

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A good beginning to the day is a morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiled or fried, this is a classic morning dish.

clue.text: Reformed gambler?

explanation.surface: A gambler who has turned over a new leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Improved means reformed, and one who bets or wagers is a gambler.

clue.text: A top man some think irreplaceable

indicators.note: some of the word means only part of it is used

explanation.surface: A star player whom people think cannot be replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert or champion performer, a crack hand at something.

clue.text: The song "Many an Adieu"

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
ta-ta is a casual British goodbye

explanation.surface: A ballad titled with a long farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a sung work for voices and instruments.

clue.text: Splashdown!

parts.note: sounds like a spacecraft landing at sea, but literally water crashing downwards

explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large waterfall where water plunges steeply.

clue.text: Notice present and hold on

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
here means present, as in a register

explanation.surface: Observe the gift and keep a grip on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast or cling.

clue.text: Subjects for those people taking directions

parts.note: them refers to those people
E for east, a compass direction
S for south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: People being told the way become the topics of conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Themes are the topics or subjects of a work or discussion.

clue.text: The small company thousand people backed last month got going

parts.note: Co is a small or shortened form of company
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
men means people

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards, so the abbreviated month is read in reverse

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the last month of the year

explanation.surface: A small firm launched in December with investors' support.
explanation.definitionFit: Commenced means began or started, so got under way.

clue.text: Omits to change, though somewhat damp

indicators.note: the word given is told to change, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone neglects to switch something, though it's a little wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet.

clue.text: Bird with the French name

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: A bird bearing a French name.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or person's rank.

clue.text: The foolish snipe at the wise

indicators.note: foolish suggests the letters behave madly and get jumbled

explanation.surface: Fools take shots at clever people.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means wise or learned, from Latin sapere, to be wise.

clue.text: Beast keeping capture dark

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the beast's word encloses the capture

parts.note: a brute is a beast
to net is to capture

explanation.surface: An animal holding its catch in the darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with dark brown hair.

clue.text: Seating offering firm support

parts.note: set means firm, as in set jelly
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Furniture providing solid backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a piece of furniture for sitting on.
